title: A Garden for the Tide
premise: Ines Ravensworth has spent eleven years building a careful life: a bookshop, a daughter, and a locked box of unsent letters to the one person who left town the night everything broke. When a flood-damaged letter surfaces — one Ines never sent, postmarked the week of the disappearance — it forces open the truth about what really happened at Ravensworth Pier, and who paid the price so Ines could survive. The letter's recipient, Wren Calloway, returns to town to sell their late mother's house, and every rehearsed sentence Ines has guarded for a decade finally demands to be spoken. In the end, Ines chooses truth over the loyalty that kept them silent, confesses their role in the old betrayal, and loses the shop but keeps Wren — learning that a heart, unlike a garden, cannot be contained, only tended.
about_author: Elodie Nystrom is a former coastal bookseller who writes love stories about people who mistake silence for safety. She lives in a drafty house above a tideline, where she keeps a garden that floods every spring and refuses to die.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A winter storm floods the bookshop's cellar, and among the ruined stock Ines finds a letter they wrote eleven years ago and never mailed — its contents half-legible, its postmark impossible. Ines burns to destroy it but hides it instead. The beat is dread disguised as routine: the past has a tide, and it is coming in.

chapters.title: The Returned
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren comes back to Saltmere to empty their mother's house, expecting indifference from Ines and finding instead a bookshop that keeps their favorite novels in stock — a decade of quiet devotion neither will name. A near-confession over tea is interrupted by the town council, who want Wren's land for a marina. The beat is longing sharpened by the suspicion that Ines knows something.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The letter surfaces publicly — the councilman who orchestrated the old cover-up uses it to blackmail Ines into supporting the marina, threatening Ines's daughter's custody. Ines finally speaks the rehearsed sentence to Wren: the truth about the night at the pier, the lie that protected a powerful family, and the love that made silence feel like survival. The beat is the climax: truth spoken, loyalty shattered, everything at stake.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Tide
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines testifies, losing the shop to legal ruin but breaking the councilman's hold on the town; Wren withdraws the land sale, gutting the marina scheme. In the flooded garden behind the old Calloway house, Ines and Wren plant something that can survive salt water. The beat is resolution: love not as containment but as tending — a heart that floods and grows anyway.
